questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: My birthday is ____ 14 November.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: The shop opens ____ 9 a.m.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: It is very cold here ____ January.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: She has been working here ____ 2018.
option_feedback: *from 2018* needs an end point or a different tense.
*has been working in 2018* does not fit.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The mango was divided ____ the two brothers.
option_feedback: *divided with* is not the usual phrase.
*into* tells the parts, not the people.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The boy jumped ____ the river to save the puppy.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: We walked ____ the river bank for an hour.
option_feedback: *across* means from one side to the other.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: This poem was written ____ Rabindranath Tagore.
option_feedback: *with* names an instrument, not the writer.
*of* does not show who did the action.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: He cut the cake ____ a knife.
option_feedback: *by* names the doer; an instrument takes *with*.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Please reach the hall ____ time; the ceremony starts at ten sharp.
option_feedback: *at time* is not a fixed phrase.
*by time* is not a fixed phrase.
*in time* means early enough for something; punctual is *on time*.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: She is very interested ____ classical music.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: The success of the event depends ____ the weather.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: ____ English, he knows French and German.
option_feedback: *beside* means next to; *besides* means in addition to.
*Except* would mean he does not know English.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: He sat ____ his friend in the class.
option_feedback: *besides* means in addition to; *beside* means next to.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: ____ the doctor, he will be fine in a week.
option_feedback: *Instead of the doctor* changes the meaning.
The meaning is *as the doctor says*.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: ____ it was raining heavily, the match continued.
option_feedback: The ideas contrast, not cause and effect.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The flight was delayed ____ the fog.
option_feedback: *because* needs a clause; *the fog* is a noun phrase.
*so* shows a result, not a cause.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: She studied hard ____ she could get a scholarship.
option_feedback: *because* gives a reason; *could get* shows purpose.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: It was ____ hot that we could not go out.
option_feedback: *too* is not followed by *that* in this pattern.
*such* needs a noun: *such a hot day*.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The roads were wet; ____, the race was postponed.
option_feedback: *moreover* adds a point; here it is a result.
A wet road causes the delay: result, not contrast.
*although* joins clauses, not sentences after a semicolon.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: He is rich; ____, he lives a simple life.
option_feedback: Being rich does not cause a simple life: contrast.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Take an umbrella ____ it rains.
option_feedback: *unless it rains* gives the wrong meaning.
You don't take an umbrella to make it rain.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: ____ being tired, she helped her mother.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: Wait here ____ I come back.
option_feedback: *by* is a deadline preposition, not a time clause joiner.
*since* needs a perfect tense in the main clause.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: You can borrow my bike ____ you return it by evening.
option_feedback: Returning it is a condition, not a purpose.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: She not only sings ____ also plays the tabla.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: It was ____ a beautiful sight that we took many photos.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: Neither the principal nor the teachers ____ aware of the change.
option_feedback: Plural nearer subject, and the context is past.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: If I ____ you, I would accept the offer.
option_feedback: In formal English, *If I were you* is the fixed form.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: She ____ have reached home by now; she left two hours ago.
option_feedback: The evidence suggests she has reached.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: ____ of the two candidates was selected; both were rejected.
option_feedback: *Both … was* is wrong, and both were rejected.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: He asked me ____ I could lend him my notes.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: I have ____ money left; I cannot buy the book.
option_feedback: *a little* is positive; you cannot buy the book.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The doctor advised him ____ sweets.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: By the time the police arrived, the robbers ____.
option_feedback: The escape happened first: past perfect.
The story is in the past.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The number of mobile users ____ increasing rapidly.
Fill in the blank with the correct option: ____ Ganga and the Yamuna meet at Prayagraj.

option_feedback: The ban is already in place; *have been banned* fits best.

State whether the following statement is true or false: *Despite* can be followed by a noun or an -ing form.
option_feedback: Not quite. *Despite the rain*, *despite being tired*.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false: *Unless* means *if … not*.
questions.explanation: *Unless you hurry* = *If you do not hurry*.
option_feedback: Correct! *Unless you hurry* = *If you do not hurry*.
Not quite. *Unless you hurry* = *If you do not hurry*.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false: *by Friday* shows a deadline.
questions.explanation: *Submit it by Friday* = not later than Friday.
option_feedback: Correct! *Submit it by Friday* = not later than Friday.
Not quite. *Submit it by Friday* = not later than Friday.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false: *Because of* is followed by a full clause.
questions.explanation: *because of* + noun: *because of the rain*; *because* + clause: *because it rained*.
option_feedback: Not quite. *because of* + noun: *because of the rain*; *because* + clause: *because it rained*.
Correct! *because of* + noun: *because of the rain*; *because* + clause: *because it rained*.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false: You should read the whole passage before filling the blanks.
questions.explanation: Later sentences often show the tense and meaning.
option_feedback: Correct! Later sentences often show the tense and meaning.
Not quite. Later sentences often show the tense and meaning.
